model.rationale: The forecast rests on the district's 20-point Democratic lean, reinforced by Neguse's overwhelming financial advantage over a challenger with no reported fundraising and by market pricing that leaves the Republican with almost no path. overview:
Joe Neguse seeks another term in a Boulder-area district that leans Democratic by about 20 points. He has raised more than $3.2 million and holds a similar cash advantage, while Republican Kelley Dennison has reported no fundraising totals. Prediction markets give the Democratic side roughly a 98 percent chance of holding the seat, and no outside groups have targeted the race.

No public general-election polling is available, so the outlook rests on district fundamentals, the incumbent's financial edge, and market pricing. A Libertarian candidate also appears on the ballot, which may trim the major-party margin slightly. The race is rated Safe Democratic, with the main uncertainty coming from the absence of recent survey data rather than any sign of a competitive contest.
